before: Campaign contracts are validated read-only and managed execution preserves one task/worktree, but execute_loop_plan returns after one managed task and retains no campaign-wide selection or consumption checkpoint.
after: An explicit foreground campaign invocation freezes one validated contract revision, persists cumulative controller state, resumes authoritative managed work before deterministic allowlisted selection, and advances serially after a task reaches its existing completed/cleaned lifecycle state.

entrypoints: loop/go-loop with the same optional flags
public_interface.compatibility: Calls without --campaign keep the existing single-task and legacy batch behavior byte-for-byte at the routing boundary.
public_interface.resume: The generated resume arguments retain the campaign contract and workspace root; controller state binds the canonical contract digest and refuses silent mandate drift.

edges: new -> running after repository-bound contract validation and immutable snapshot
running -> task_in_progress after deterministic selection and persisted intent
task_in_progress -> running only after existing task lifecycle returns task_complete/done
running/task_in_progress -> budget_exhausted when cumulative wall/task/attempt ceiling is reached
running -> no_eligible_tasks when no permitted eligible task exists; this is never goal_verified
state_model.authority: Task status, managed run state, workspace registry, release receipt and outcome evidence remain canonical; campaign state records selection/consumption/provenance but never copies authoritative outcome status.

selection_precedence: One permitted active managed task with a durable checkpoint
One permitted delivered task with pending release/cleanup checkpoint
First eligible open task in authority.permitted_tasks order
Skip task-local dependency, decision or readiness blockers and record reasons; continue scanning unrelated permitted tasks
Fail closed on foreign active work, missing active checkpoint, conflicting controller, unsafe repository or unresolved external effect

budget.resume_rule: Consumption is monotonic for the frozen campaign digest and cannot reset by process restart or CLI retry.

non_goals: No daemon, timer, background service or unattended trigger
No parallel builders, multi-host scheduling or new worker adapter
No hidden global queue or copied task/outcome lifecycle
No inferred publication/deployment authority and no repeated unknown external effect
No claim that task exhaustion proves the vision or campaign goal
No change to existing behavior when --campaign is absent
evidence_plan: Public-interface RED/GREEN tests for serial advancement and durable resume
Negative tests for deterministic allowlist order, task-local skip, mandate drift, cumulative budget and unsafe active state
Existing managed resume/worktree regressions and full make check
Fresh critic and architecture conformance against the final candidate before integration/release
reasoning: This is the smallest compatible placement: campaign_contracts retains immutable authority validation, run_state retains task/process ownership, task_state remains the task index, and the new campaign module owns only serial orchestration and its durable audit checkpoint.
